Oracle Planning Member Properties – Complete Impact Lab + Explain + Financial Statement Impact
Change a property → observe the numeric impact → understand why
Hands-On v7 • Images + Explain + BISP Branding

Do not memorize properties. Change them and watch the numbers move.

This tested version turns the supplied Oracle Planning member-property screens and Account_Behaviour.xlsx into a practical metadata laboratory. All interactive engines are initialized in-browser and recalculate their numeric tables immediately when students change properties or input values. Students can change selected properties and immediately see the effect in numeric tables.

Values such as Jan/Feb/Mar 100/120/150, rates 94.8/95.4/94.8, Forecast Sep FY26–Sep FY27 and Working/Target examples come from the supplied workbook/screenshots. Where the lab offers an alternative property setting not shown in the screenshot, it is clearly an educational simulation to demonstrate impact.

Complete Property Coverage: The new “All Properties” tab under each dimension now includes every property visible in the supplied Member Properties screens plus the visible UDA, Member Formula and Attribute Values tabs where applicable. Direct calculation properties show numeric effects; metadata-only properties show measurable operational impacts such as cube visibility, workflow completion, security level, dynamic-child capacity or rule-selection scope.

Account Dimension Assignment

Use the screenshot first, then change the properties/assumptions below. The financial statements recalculate immediately so you can distinguish metadata impact from data-input impact.

Student deliverable: Record the property changed, the numeric before/after result, and explain which statement changed and why.

Assignment 1 — Account Properties and Three-Statement Impact

  1. Change Revenue Time Balance from Flow to Last.
  2. Change Variance Reporting from Non-Expense to Expense.
  3. Change Revenue growth assumption and observe P&L.
  4. Change AR collection assumption and observe Balance Sheet/Cash Flow.
  5. Explain why a metadata change can create a reporting error even when monthly source data is unchanged.
Student answer: Why is Flow normally more appropriate than Last for Revenue?
Source screenshot: Entity 110 Facilities Resources, Base Currency USD.

Assignment 2 — Entity Properties and Group Financial Statements

  1. Change an entity Base Currency.
  2. Change Entity aggregation from Addition to Ignore.
  3. Observe how entity-level Revenue and Cash affect group P&L and Balance Sheet.
  4. Explain why Cash Flow also changes when the translated cash movement changes.

Assignment 4 — Version Properties: Working, Target and Sandbox

  1. Change Working regional values.
  2. Compare to Target.
  3. Add a private Sandbox adjustment.
  4. Publish or discard it.
  5. Observe P&L, Balance Sheet cash and Cash Flow before and after publish.

Final Hands-On Activities — Property Changes to P&L, Balance Sheet & Cash Flow

These activities deliberately connect metadata choices with a small financial model. Students should change one property at a time, observe the numeric effect, and explain the accounting/planning consequence.

Change Property
Observe P&L
Observe Balance Sheet
Observe Cash Flow
Explain Impact

Hands-On 1 — Account Time Balance: Revenue vs Cash

Question: Why is Flow usually logical for Revenue but Last is usually logical for Cash?

Hands-On 2 — Entity Base Currency & Aggregation

Hands-On 3 — Scenario Window, BegBal and Rate Table

Hands-On 4 — Version Working vs Target + Sandbox

Hands-On 5 — Integrated Three-Statement Challenge

Challenge: Change at least four planning assumptions/properties. Keep closing cash above 450 and make the Balance Sheet balance.

Assignment 5 — Integrated Planning Three-Statement Challenge

Goal: Combine Account, Entity, Scenario and Version choices into a miniature driver-based financial model. Make the Balance Sheet balance and reconcile closing cash to the Cash Flow statement.

Assignment deliverable: Change at least four properties/assumptions so Revenue grows by 10%, closing cash stays above 450, and the Balance Sheet remains balanced. Document what you changed and why.
